title: Task structure and construct validity in the neurobiology of trust: A systematic structural synthesis
title_zh: 任务结构与构念效度在信任神经生物学中的系统结构合成
abstract: The neuroscience of interpersonal trust has expanded across functional magnetic resonance imaging, electroencephalography, functional near-infrared spectroscopy, pharmacology, genetics, physiology, and brain stimulation. Although this literature implicates distributed reward-, salience-, mentalizing-, and executive-control systems, findings are often difficult to compare because nominally similar Trust Game paradigms differ in their task architecture and analytic definition of trust. Here, we provided a PRISMA-guided systematic structural synthesis of 198 empirical studies comprising 200 experiments. Rather than conducting an effect-size or coordinate-based meta-analysis, we coded paradigm architecture, economic structure, temporal dynamics, trustee information, control conditions, participant populations, measurement modalities, and analytic strategies to characterize conditions relevant to neurobiological interpretation. Our synthesis showed that trust neuroscience is dominated by standard and binary Trust Game variants, simulated partners, limited explicit controls, and decision- and outcome-phase analyses. Exploratory contingency analyses identified associations among task architecture, measurement approach, and analytic operationalization without testing neurobiological effects. These features may emphasize different trust-related processes, including valuation of expected reciprocity, betrayal aversion under vulnerability, social inference about partner intentions, executive regulation, and feedback-based updating. We therefore propose a structural-computational alignment framework in which neurobiological findings can be interpreted relative to the task features and analytic contrasts under which they are observed. This framework reframes heterogeneity in trust neuroscience as a construct-validity problem rather than simple theoretical fragmentation. Explicit alignment among task design, inferred computation, analytic choices, and neurobiological measures may support a coherent mechanistic account of interpersonal trust.
abstract_zh: 人际信任的神经科学已扩展至功能磁共振成像、脑电图、功能近红外光谱、药理学、遗传学、生理学和脑刺激等多种技术。虽然这些文献涉及分布式的奖励、显著性、心理化和执行控制系统，但由于名义上相似的信任游戏范式在任务架构和信任的分析定义上存在差异，研究结果往往难以直接比较。本文基于PRISMA指南，对198项实证研究（共200个实验）进行了系统结构合成。我们并未进行效应量或坐标基础的荟萃分析，而是对范式架构、经济结构、时间动态、受托人信息、对照条件、参与者人群、测量方式和分析策略进行了编码，以描述与神经生物学解释相关的条件。合成结果显示，信任神经科学主要由标准和二元信任游戏变体、模拟伙伴、有限的显式对照以及决策期和结果期分析所主导。探索性条件分析揭示了任务架构、测量方法和分析操作化之间的关联，但未检验神经生物学效应。这些特征可能强调不同的信任相关过程，包括对预期互惠的评估、在脆弱状态下的背叛厌恶、对伙伴意图的社会推理、执行调节以及基于反馈的更新。因此，我们提出了一个结构-计算对齐框架，在该框架中，神经生物学发现可以相对于其观察到的任务特征和分析对比进行解释。该框架将信任神经科学中的异质性重新定义为构念效度问题，而非简单的理论碎片化。任务设计、推断计算、分析选择和神经生物学测量之间的明确对齐，可能支持对人际信任的连贯机制性解释。
